member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Rendering.Svg.SvgRenderer
member.summary: Renders components and whole documents to SVG vector graphics.
member.remarks: The SVG is built in memory and written to the output stream asynchronously, so the renderer works with streams that disallow synchronous I/O (e.g. an ASP.NET response body).

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Rendering.Svg.SvgRenderer.RenderGroupedByLayerAsync(OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbComponent,System.IO.Stream,OriginalCircuit.Eda.Rendering.RenderOptions,OriginalCircuit.Altium.Rendering.PcbViewSide,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Renders a single PCB component (footprint), same as , except each PCB layer's primitives are wrapped in a named SVG group (<g id="layer-33">). A front-end can then toggle individual layers on/off client-side, with no server round-trip — the same trick uses for its physical (substrate/copper/soldermask/...) groups.
member.param: The stream the SVG is written to.
Which side's layers to include; (the default) shows every layer the footprint uses, which is usually what you want for a library footprint.
member.returns: The distinct PCB layer IDs that were drawn, in the order their groups appear in the SVG — pass each through / to build a layer-visibility UI.

member.summary: Renders a whole PCB document (board) as a photorealistic 2D SVG (a fab-house / gerber-viewer look) rather than the Altium-editor view. Configure the solder-mask, copper, silkscreen, finish and substrate colours via ; null uses the default green-mask / ENIG / white preset. The supersample knob is ignored for vector output.
member.param: Appearance (colours, viewed side, finish); null uses the default preset.
